USMLE-style practice · Pathology

Minimal inflammation around dying cells

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A tissue section shows scattered shrunken cells with condensed chromatin and small membrane-bound fragments. Adjacent phagocytes contain some of the fragments, and there is little surrounding inflammation. Which feature best explains this limited inflammatory response?

  1. Cell contents remain contained during prompt phagocytic clearance
  2. All intracellular enzymes have permanently disappeared
  3. Plasma membranes rupture early in every affected cell
  4. Neutrophils cannot enter any tissue undergoing apoptosis
  5. The dying cells increase ATP production indefinitely
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Cell contents remain contained during prompt phagocytic clearance

Apoptotic fragments are packaged and removed before substantial leakage.

Understanding the options

Cell contents remain contained during prompt phagocytic clearance
Apoptotic fragments are packaged and removed before substantial leakage.
All intracellular enzymes have permanently disappeared
Enzyme disappearance is not the reason apoptotic cells are relatively noninflammatory.
Plasma membranes rupture early in every affected cell
Early rupture favors inflammation and is characteristic of necrotic injury.
Neutrophils cannot enter any tissue undergoing apoptosis
This absolute exclusion is not a property of apoptosis.
The dying cells increase ATP production indefinitely
Apoptosis does not require indefinite ATP production.
